source_text: [1] Ταῦτα δὲ παραινῶ ὑμῖν, ἀγαπητοί, εἰδὼς ὅτι καὶ ὑμεῖς οὕτως ἔχετε. προφυλάσσω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τῶν θηρίων τῶν ἀνθρωπομόρφων, οὓς οὐ μόνον δεῖ ὑμᾶς μὴ παραδέχεσθαι, ἀλλ’ εἰ δυνατὸν μηδὲ συναντᾶν, μόνον δὲ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν, ἐάν πως μετανοήσωσιν, ὅπερ δύσκολον, τούτου δὲ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὸ ἀληθινὸν ἡμῶν ζῆν. 2, εἰ γὰρ τὸ δοκεῖν ταῦτα ἐπράχθη ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν, κἀγὼ τὸ δοκεῖν δέδεμαι. τί δὲ καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἔκδοτον δέδωκα τῷ θανάτῳ, πρὸς πῦρ, πρὸς μάχαιραν, πρὸς θηρία; ἀλλ’ ἐγγὺς μαχαίρας ἐγγὺς θεοῦ, μεταξὺ θηρίων μεταξὺ θεοῦ: μόνον ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τὸ συμπαθεῖν αὐτῷ πάντα ὑπομένω, αὐτοῦ με ἐνδυναμοῦντος τοῦ τελείου ἀνθρώπου.
pass_a_gloss: [1] I urge these things on you, beloved, knowing that you too are of this mind. But I guard you in advance against the beasts in human form, whom you must not only not receive but, if possible, not even meet; only pray for them, if somehow they may repent, which is hard. But Jesus Christ, our true life, has authority over this. [2] For if these things were done by our Lord in appearance, I too am in chains in appearance. And why have I given myself up to death, to fire, to sword, to beasts? But near the sword, near God; in the midst of beasts, in the midst of God; only in the name of Jesus Christ do I endure all things, so as to suffer with him, while he himself, the perfect man, gives me strength.
pass_b_english: I urge this on you, dear friends, knowing that you think as I do. But I am guarding you ahead of time against beasts in human shape. You must not welcome them. If you can, do not even meet them. Only pray for them, in case they might somehow repent. That is hard. But Jesus Christ, our true life, has power over it.

If what our Lord did was only an appearance, then my chains are only an appearance too. Then why have I handed myself over to death, to fire, to the sword, to wild beasts? No: near the sword is near God. Among the beasts is among God. Only in the name of Jesus Christ do I bear everything, so that I may suffer with him; and he, the perfect man, gives me strength (Philippians 4:13).

choices.why: Ignatius's own image, kept; the irony lands against the real beasts he faces in §2.

choices.term: ἐγγὺς μαχαίρας ἐγγὺς θεοῦ, μεταξὺ θηρίων μεταξὺ θεοῦ
choices.english: near the sword is near God. Among the beasts is among God.
choices.why: Verbless paired bursts kept as bursts; 'among God' keeps the deliberate oddity of the parallel.
rejected: in company with God (ANF; flattens the parallel)

choices.why: Articular infinitive 'our true living' in natural English.
Lake's text has no participle; 'who became' (ANF) reflects another reading.
rejected: who became a perfect man (not in this text)

anf_compare.notes: Same overall sense. ANF 'He who became a perfect man' and 'in company with God' do not match Lake's Greek, which reads 'the perfect man' and the bare parallel 'among beasts, among God'.

bible_refs.note: 'he strengthens me' (endynamountos me) echoes Paul's 'through him who strengthens me'.

notes: Span: whole of Smyrnaeans 4 (sections 1); old ANF span covers the full chapter.

Romans 8:17 (suffer with him) is a possible echo, but Paul uses sympaschomen, not sympathein; left out of inline refs.
Repair 2026-10-02: μόνον ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ now qualifies ὑπομένω ('Only in the name of Jesus Christ do I bear everything'); the added wish 'let it be' is removed.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] checked clause by clause. Greek «Ταῦτα δὲ παραινῶ ὑμῖν, ἀγαπητοί, εἰδὼς ὅτι καὶ ὑμεῖς οὕτως ἔχετε» matches A «I urge these things on you, beloved, knowing that you too are of this mind» and B «I urge this on you, dear friends, knowing that you think as I do». Negation held: «οὐ μόνον δεῖ ὑμᾶς μὴ παραδέχεσθαι, ἀλλ’ εἰ δυνατὸν μηδὲ συναντᾶν» = A «must not only not receive but, if possible, not even meet» and B «must not welcome them. If you can, do not even meet them»; «μόνον δὲ προσεύχεσθε» kept. Agency and modality kept for «τούτου δὲ ἔχει ἐξουσίαν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὸ ἀληθινὸν ἡμῶν ζῆν» and «ἑαυτὸν ἔκδοτον δέδωκα». Docetic hypothesis «εἰ γὰρ τὸ δοκεῖν ταῦτα ἐπράχθη ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν, κἀγὼ τὸ δοκεῖν δέδεμαι» is not reversed in A «in appearance» or B «only an appearance». «ἐγγὺς μαχαίρας ἐγγὺς θεοῦ, μεταξὺ θηρίων μεταξὺ θεοῦ» and «αὐτοῦ με ἐνδυναμοῦντος τοῦ τελείου ἀνθρώπου» kept; B’s «(Philippians 4:13)» matches the supplied wording note for ἐνδυναμοῦντος, not a shifted verse. Title names the thought, not a locus. Inline «2,» is noted, not dropped.

Paragraph 1: Locked Greek fully rendered in both Pass A and B. Pass A: 'I urge these things on you, beloved, knowing that you too are of this mind. But I guard you in advance against the beasts in human form...' matches Greek '[1] Ταῦτα δὲ παραινῶ ὑμῖν, ἀγαπητοί, εἰδὼς ὅτι καὶ ὑμεῖς οὕτως ἔχετε. προφυλάσσω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τῶν θηρίων τῶν ἀνθρωπομόρφων...'. Pass B conveys same sense with slight rephrasing ('I urge this on you, dear friends... guarding you ahead of time against beasts in human shape'). No omission, addition, or contradiction. Negation: 'οὐ μόνον... ἀλλ’' rendered as 'not only... but' in A and 'not welcome... do not even meet' in B — agency and modality preserved. Modality: 'εἰ δυνατὸν μηδὲ συναντᾶν' → 'if possible, not even meet' (A), 'If you can, do not even meet them' (B) — correct. Doctrine: Christ’s authority over repentance and strength affirmed. Scripture: Pass B adds '(Philippians 4:13)' as an allusion (supported by notes: 'he strengthens me' echoes Paul); this is an allowed added identification, not a false citation. Title 'Near the Sword, Near God' reflects the thought of ἐγγὺς μαχαίρας ἐγγὺς θεοῦ, μεταξὺ θηρίων μεταξὺ θεοῦ — not just locus. Notes disclose OCR/marker handling (§2 inside §1 with '2,').
